name: Electrical goods (fans, cables, switches, lighting)

problems.words: Before summer everyone wants fans and we can't produce enough
quick_ideas: Look back at last season's sales by model and week — shows when demand really starts
Set a target stock by model before the season — turns guesses into a plan.

workzap_build.text: a seasonal build plan by model and week with progress against plan every day.

problems.ask_first: When do you start building stock for the season?
problems.free_stops: How targets are set from history is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many fan orders arrived after you ran out last summer, so pre-season production can match the real rush.
Give one supervisor a weekly notebook for fan stockouts by model, so the factory adds the right fans earlier.

problems.words: After summer, thousands of fans sit in the warehouse
quick_ideas: List leftover stock by model and age — shows what to clear first
Offer dealers early-order terms for next season's carry-over — moves stock sooner.

workzap_build.text: stock cover by model with alerts when production is running ahead of sales late in the season.

problems.ask_first: What happened to leftover stock last year?
problems.free_stops: Cover levels and alert timing are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count leftover fans by model and carton condition in one warehouse walk, so you see which stock is hardest to move.
Give one storekeeper one notebook for slow fan models and a fixed Friday review, so carry-over gets flagged early.

problems.words: Copper prices jump and my cable price list is wrong overnight
quick_ideas: Put an issue date on every price list — dealers know which one is current
Recost your top cable sizes at today's copper rate — shows where you're losing.

workzap_build.text: one live price list per dealer tier, sent to dealers right away when copper rates change.

problems.ask_first: How do dealers find out about new prices today?
problems.free_stops: Pricing rules and the publishing set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare today's cable buying cost against the latest list for your fastest sizes, so you spot which prices are already stale.
Give one person the job of marking one current cable price list each morning, so dealers get the same latest rates.

problems.words: Warranty claims come back but we can't tell if they're real
quick_ideas: Start recording the serial and dispatch dealer for every unit — gives you a date to check claims against
Ask for photos with each claim — screens out obvious misuse.

workzap_build.text: You would see dealers scanning the serial and uploading photos for each warranty claim, checked against dispatch records so genuine claims stand out.

problems.ask_first: Are serial numbers printed on every unit?
problems.free_stops: The serial capture and claim-check rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many warranty returns mention the same fan or light model this month, so doubtful claims and repeat complaints separate quickly.
Give one service desk person one register for every claim by model and dealer role, so repeat patterns stop getting missed.

problems.words: Dealers send back fakes with our name for repair
quick_ideas: Keep a few genuine and fake samples side by side for your service desk — staff learn the differences
Record where fakes are showing up — shows which areas need attention.

workzap_build.text: a genuine-product check where a code on the box can be verified on WhatsApp by dealers or customers.

problems.ask_first: Which areas are fakes showing up in?
problems.free_stops: The code design setup is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which product lines and market areas bring the most fake returns this month, so staff know where checks matter most.
Give one counter person one shelf for doubtful returns awaiting review, so fake repair items stop mixing with genuine ones.

problems.words: Each dealer has a different discount and nobody remembers what was promised
quick_ideas: Write every dealer's agreed discount in one list — ends "I was promised"
Group dealers into a few tiers — makes it simpler to manage.

workzap_build.text: a dealer ledger with tier, discount, scheme and credit on one record, applied directly to orders.

problems.ask_first: How many active dealers do you have?
problems.free_stops: Tier rules are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the discounts actually given this week against the agreed dealer list, so margin leaks and promise disputes show up fast.
Give one sales coordinator one master discount list and a fixed handover time, so every rep quotes from the same record.

problems.words: Sales reps take orders on WhatsApp and some never reach the factory
quick_ideas: Make one order number the only channel — nothing gets lost in personal chats
Confirm every order back to the rep — catches misses the same day.

workzap_build.text: You would see reps sending their orders into one order book, with the status of each order sent back to the rep.

problems.ask_first: How many reps are in the field?
problems.free_stops: The order flow is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many rep orders reached dispatch versus how many were mentioned in chats today, so missed factory orders show.
Give one dispatcher one notebook for all rep orders received by day, so factory handover stops slipping through chats.

problems.words: Service centre tickets are in a register and nobody follows up
quick_ideas: Go through open tickets once and close or chase each one — clears the backlog
Note fault type per model — shows which models fail most.

workzap_build.text: a service ticket tracker with turnaround time and repeat faults by model.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many tickets come in during the season?
problems.free_stops: The ticket flow and reports are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open service tickets by age and fault type in one register check, so the oldest customer issues stand out today.
Give one person the job of reviewing the service register every afternoon, so pending follow-ups get chased before they go cold.

problems.words: I don't know daily sales by region until month-end
quick_ideas: Ask for a weekly regional total — gets you closer than month-end
Choose the few numbers you want daily — keeps it focused.

workzap_build.text: a morning read of sales by region and model, stock cover, warranty claims and receivables.

problems.ask_first: Where is sales data entered today?
problems.free_stops: Which figures feed the daily read is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each region's sales note arrival time for the past week, so you see which areas delay your daily view.
Give one person one daily cut-off for regional totals in one notebook, so month-end surprises shrink into a routine.

never_say: No electrical safety, wiring, load-rating or certification advice.
Never say a product meets or fails a standard.
Never help put false certification marks, fake ratings or another brand's name on products; decline.
Shocks, electrical fires or burns: stop and point to emergency services.
Never help dispose of stolen copper or under-invoice imports; decline.
No customer or electrician names or numbers in registers; roles only.

sample_reply.person: Koi hal batao. Summer mein pankhay pooray nahi hotay aur September ke baad godown bhara hota hai.
sample_reply.pi:
Ji haan, shuruaat chhoti si ho sakti hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, pichle saal ki sales model aur hafte ke hisaab se dekhein, taake pata chale demand asal mein kab shuru hoti hai.
Doosra, season se pehle har model ka stock target tay karein, taake planning andaze se na ho.
Is ko mazboot karne ke liye Workzap ye de sakta hai: model-wise season build plan jo roz dikhaye ke plan ke muqable kahan khade hain.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
